```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)
library(tidyverse)
library(knitr)
library(lubridate)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
```

I am choosing option 2 for the homework and recreate the graph of homicide data.

## Clean the Data and get homicide counts for each month

```{r}
homicides <- read.csv("homicide-data.csv")

homicides <- homicides %>% mutate(city_name = paste(city, state, sep = ", "))

homicides <- homicides %>% select(-lat, -lon, -city, -state)

homicides <- homicides %>% filter(city_name == "Baltimore, MD")

homicides <- homicides %>% mutate(reported_date = ymd(reported_date))

homicides <- homicides %>% mutate(year = year(reported_date), month = month(reported_date, label = TRUE))

homicidecounts <- homicides %>% count(year, month, name = "row_count")

homicidecounts <- homicidecounts %>% mutate(date = paste(month, year, sep = " "))

homicidecounts$date <- my(homicidecounts$date)

homicidecounts$season <- ifelse(homicidecounts$month %in% c("Nov", "Dec", "Jan", "Feb", "Mar", "Apr"), "Winter", "Summer")
```

## Graph the data

```{r}
ggplot(homicidecounts) + 
  geom_col(aes(x = date, y = row_count, fill = season)) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Winter" = "lightgray", "Summer" = "lightblue")) +
  scale_x_date(date_breaks = "1 year") +
  labs(y = "Monthly homicides",
       x = "Date") +
  ggtitle("Homicides in Baltimore, MD") +
  theme_dark()

```
